messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Japanese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Japanese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
人生の道の真ん中で 暗い森の中で自分を見つけた、 正しい道が失われていた。

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Japanese) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Nel | marks location inside a larger span | で | “in/at” | OK | | mezzo | the central point of a stretch | 真ん中 | “middle” | OK | | del | genitive linking “mezzo” to “cammin” | の | “of” | OK | | cammin | the path taken through life | 道 | “road / way” | OK | | di | links “cammin” to “nostra vita” | の | “of” | OK | | nostra | belonging to the speaker and companions | 人生 | “life (our)” | OK | | vita | the span of human existence | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (already expressed by 人生) | | mi | the speaker as the experiencer of the verb | 自分 | “self / oneself” | OK | | ritrovai | the act of encountering oneself in a place | 見つけた | “found” | OK | | per | indicates the spatial context of the encounter | 中で | “inside / within” | OK | | una | non‑specific forest | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (indefinite article omitted) | | selva | a dark, wooded area | 森 | “forest / wood” | OK | | oscura | lacking light, metaphorically confusing | 暗い | “dark” | OK | | ché | introduces causal clause | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (cause omitted in Japanese) | | la | specifies a particular way | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (definite article omitted) | | diritta | the correct, direct path | 正しい | “right / correct” | OK | | via | the intended route through life | 道 | “way / road” | OK | | era | copular verb linking subject to predicate | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (copula not needed) | | smarrita | the state of being not found or gone astray | 失われていた | “had been lost / missed” | OK |
---
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: `vita`, `una`, `ché`, `la`, `era` – these function words or articles are naturally omitted in Japanese. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.
All remaining source tokens have appropriate Japanese equivalents that preserve the meaning of the reference translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Japanese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
